excerpt: Automation must be rethought for the construction industry
content_html:
In an era increasingly dominated by AI and automation, it’s still incredible just how much construction work remains manual. The contrast is most stark in data centers – facilities built to power cutting-edge technology, but whose delivery is generally still slowed down by major fragmentation and time-consuming manual tasks.

One of the industry’s biggest challenges seems to be capturing and understanding what’s actually happening on a project. Project managers can spend countless hours walking sites, checking completed work and coordinating contractors operating to different schedules. When documentation falls behind, small issues can go unnoticed and eventually develop into costly delays.

While the industry is finally starting to get to grips with this technology, construction is presenting own on challenges. Autonomy works best within fixed parameters and with a limited number of variables, but live sites offer the opposite – changing plans, moving materials, new structures being built and multiple trades working alongside each other.

Construction is where automation fails – is now the turning point?

These are the exact conditions that have made automation ineffective in construction. But automation isn’t impractical or impossible, it just means vendors will need to focus on the tasks where machines can deliver the best results.

Progress capturing, side documentation and routine inspections are some of the areas where automation could work best, and better still, companies like OpenSpace argue much of this work can actually be done outside of normal operating hours to both reduce disruption, and to reduce exposure to a live and dynamic environment.

Data centers could be a good proving ground for this, with large floor plans, repeatable layouts and intense schedule pressures. With up-to-date data from overnight checks, for example, leaders could assess progress and identify areas that need extra attention.

But collecting that data is only the first step, because the AI running behind the scenes need to be able to interpret site imagery to cross-reference it with site plans, drawings, schedules and other information held across other systems.

In this Q&A, OpenSpace CEO Jeevan Kalanithi explains why construction automation is starting to gain momentum, why ‘good enough’ may indeed be good enough without needing immediate perfection, and how automated monitoring could actually help soften the blow of ongoing labor shortages.

  • Construction has traditionally been one of the least automated industries. Why is that beginning to change now?

I actually think the idea that construction is slow to adopt technology is a bit of a misconception. Builders adopt tools that genuinely make their jobs easier – they've just been waiting for technology that understands how they actually work.

Construction is fundamentally different from industries like manufacturing. Every project is unique. Jobsites change every day. Teams are working in environments that are constantly evolving, with dozens of trades operating simultaneously. That's a much harder environment to automate than a factory or warehouse where conditions are highly controlled.

For a long time, most construction software focused on documents, schedules and reports because that's what computers could understand. But construction isn't really a document problem – it's a physical-world problem. The most important information lives on the jobsite itself: what's been built, what's changed, where work is progressing and where risks are emerging.

What's changing now is that AI is becoming capable of understanding the physical world. Instead of asking people to manually document what's happening, AI can interpret images and other real-world data to understand the state of a project. That makes robotics and automation much more practical because they fit naturally into how builders already work instead of forcing them to adopt entirely new processes.

  • Robotics in construction has been discussed for years but has seen relatively limited adoption. What factors are contributing to the increased interest in autonomous and semi-autonomous systems on jobsites today?

The conversation has become much more practical.

Ten years ago, people asked whether robots would replace construction workers or build entire buildings autonomously. Today the question is much simpler: How can robots help experienced builders work more efficiently? That's an important shift because construction has always adopted tools that solve real problems.

The biggest opportunities today are around repetitive, time-consuming tasks like documenting progress, capturing site conditions or performing routine inspections. Those activities are incredibly valuable, but they're not necessarily the best use of a superintendent's or project engineer's time.

I think of robotics a bit like the introduction of nail guns. Nail guns didn't replace carpenters – they helped carpenters work faster and more consistently. Robotics is following a similar path. The goal isn't to automate construction. It's to automate specific tasks that allow skilled professionals to spend more time coordinating work, solving problems and making decisions.

We're already seeing that with the robotics companies that we integrate with, each approaching different aspects of autonomy. Rather than trying to solve every problem, they're proving that robots can reliably perform specific tasks that create immediate value on today's jobsites.

  • Data centers and other large-scale projects have been cited as promising early use cases for construction robotics. What characteristics make those environments more suitable for autonomous technologies?

Data centers are actually a great example of where robotics and AI can demonstrate value today because they combine three characteristics that work well for autonomous systems.

First, they're relatively structured environments. Compared to a renovation project or an occupied hospital, data centers typically have large floor plates, repeatable layouts and fewer unexpected obstacles, making them easier for robots to navigate.

Second, they're incredibly schedule-sensitive. AI infrastructure is expanding at an unprecedented pace, and every day matters. Owners and contractors need continuous visibility into progress because hundreds of activities are happening simultaneously.

Finally, they're highly repetitive. The same systems and construction sequences occur over and over, which allows robotics to operate more consistently and makes it easier to measure progress over time.

Autonomous data capture is particularly valuable in these environments because it creates a consistent visual record without disrupting work during the day. That gives project teams objective information about what's actually happening on site, helping them identify issues earlier, coordinate more effectively and keep stakeholders aligned.

  • Construction sites are highly dynamic environments. What are some of the biggest technical and operational challenges robots face when deployed on active projects?

Construction sites are probably one of the hardest environments you could ask an autonomous system to operate in.

Unlike a warehouse, where everything is designed to be predictable, construction sites change constantly. Materials move. Equipment gets relocated. Walls appear. Doors that were open yesterday might be closed today. You also have dozens or sometimes hundreds of people working alongside autonomous systems, so safety has to remain the highest priority.

There are practical challenges as well. Connectivity isn't always reliable. GPS often doesn't work indoors. Navigation has to account for changing layouts and temporary obstacles that don't exist in more controlled environments.

That's why I think we'll continue seeing supervised autonomy for quite some time. Humans are still remarkably good at adapting to unexpected situations, and construction has plenty of them.

One lesson we've learned is that "good enough" often beats "technically perfect." Builders don't need the most sophisticated robot, they need one that's reliable enough to show up every day, operate safely and consistently, and fit into the way projects already run.

  • As robotics adoption grows, what role does visual intelligence play in helping machines understand and navigate the physical world?

Whether imagery comes from a person carrying a 360° camera, a robot, a drone or another autonomous system, collecting the data is really only the first step. The real challenge is understanding what that data means.

AI has become remarkably good at understanding language, but if it's going to operate in the real-world economy, it also needs to understand physical places, physical assets and physical work.

Construction has always had information about what was supposed to happen – drawings, BIM models, schedules and specifications. What's historically been much harder is understanding what actually happened in the field.

That's where visual intelligence comes in. AI can compare what's been built against what was intended to be built, measure progress over time, identify potential issues and surface insights that help project teams make better decisions.

Our philosophy is simple: we don't really care how the data gets collected. Whether it comes from a phone, a 360° camera, a drone, a laser scanner or a robotics platform from one of our robotics partners, our goal is to bring that information together into a common understanding of the jobsite.

Today, our customers have captured imagery across more than 70 billion square feet of construction. That scale creates an opportunity not only to help builders today, but also to help train and validate the next generation of AI systems that need to understand the physical world.

  • There's often concern that robotics could replace workers. How are builders currently thinking about the relationship between automation and the existing construction workforce?

I think that's a very understandable concern, but it doesn't reflect what we're seeing on jobsites.

The builders we work with aren't trying to replace experienced people. If anything, they're trying to figure out how to help those people do more.

Construction has faced labor shortages for decades, and demand continues to outpace the available workforce. There simply aren't enough skilled people entering the trades to meet the amount of work that needs to get done. That's especially true as we build more data centers, manufacturing facilities and infrastructure.

Robotics and AI help address that challenge by taking on repetitive work like routine documentation, progress capture or inspections, allowing experienced professionals to spend more time coordinating work, solving problems and applying their expertise.

The best technology doesn't replace people – it amplifies what people are already good at. That's how I think construction will continue to adopt AI-powered tools and robotics. They become another set of tools that help experienced teams make better decisions, work more efficiently and get more done with the resources they already have.

  • The concept of "human-in-the-loop" robotics is gaining attention across industries. How does that approach apply within construction environments?

I think human-in-the-loop is going to be the dominant model for construction for quite some time.

Construction is simply too dynamic to expect fully autonomous systems to handle every situation. Something unexpected happens every day – a blocked corridor, a relocated piece of equipment, a new safety barrier, an area that's suddenly inaccessible. Humans are still exceptionally good at recognizing those situations and adapting in real time.

What we're seeing today is a very practical division of responsibilities. Robots handle routine, repetitive tasks consistently, while people provide judgment, context and intervention whenever it's needed.

Some of our robotics partners are already operating this way, where autonomous systems perform most of the work but remain remotely supervised so a person can step in if something unexpected occurs.

I don't think that's a compromise. I think it's actually the right model. The goal isn't autonomy for its own sake. The goal is giving project teams better information while maintaining the flexibility and judgment that complex construction projects require.

  • Some contractors are experimenting with autonomous data capture during off-hours, such as overnight or before crews arrive. What lessons are emerging from those early deployments?

The biggest lesson has been consistency.

One of the challenges with manual documentation is that it depends on people having the time to do it. On a busy project, it's easy for documentation to become a lower priority because everyone's focused on solving immediate problems.

Autonomous capture changes that. Robots can document the site on a predictable schedule, often overnight or before crews arrive, creating a consistent visual record every day without interrupting construction activities.

That consistency gives teams a much clearer understanding of how a project is progressing over time. It also makes documentation much more resilient. If a superintendent is tied up or a project engineer is out that day, the visual record doesn't stop. Everyone still has access to current information about what's happening on site.

Capturing a visual record has always been a natural byproduct of walking a site with a 360° camera. It's also a very natural task to hand to a robot. That allows experienced people to spend more of their time interpreting information and making decisions instead of simply collecting data.

  • Looking ahead, what indicators should the industry watch to better understand whether construction robotics is moving beyond pilot programs and toward broader adoption?

I don't think the biggest indicator will be the number of robots on jobsites. It will be whether contractors keep using them after the pilot is over.

Construction is a very practical industry. Builders don't adopt technology because it's exciting, they adopt it because it saves time, reduces risk or helps projects run more smoothly. If a technology creates more work than it eliminates, it won't last.

We'll also know the industry has reached the next stage when robotics becomes just another way of collecting project information. Builders shouldn't have to think about whether data came from a person, a robot, a drone or another autonomous system. They should simply have access to an accurate, up-to-date understanding of what's happening on their projects.

Ultimately, I think the story is bigger than robotics. The real-world economy doesn't run on documents alone. It runs on physical places, physical assets and physical work. If AI is going to create value there, it has to understand reality, not just language.

That's why we say agents need eyes. When AI can reliably see, understand and reason about what's happening in the physical world, robotics becomes much more than automation. It becomes a new way for people to interact with the built environment and make better decisions. I think that's the transition we'll be talking about over the next decade.

blocks.html_en: In this Q&A, OpenSpace CEO Jeevan Kalanithi explains why construction automation is starting to gain momentum, why ‘good enough’ may indeed be good enough without needing immediate perfection, and how automated monitoring could actually help soften the blow of ongoing labor shortages.

sentences.en: In this Q&A, OpenSpace CEO Jeevan Kalanithi explains why construction automation is starting to gain momentum, why ‘good enough’ may indeed be good enough without needing immediate perfection, and how automated monitoring could actually help soften the blow of ongoing labor shortages.
sentences.zh: 在本次问答中，OpenSpace 首席执行官 Jeevan Kalanithi 解释了为什么建筑自动化开始获得发展势头，为什么“足够好”可能确实足够好而无需立即完善，以及自动化监控如何真正帮助缓解持续劳动力短缺的打击。

blocks.html_en: • Construction has traditionally been one of the least automated industries. Why is that beginning to change now?

sentences.en: Construction has traditionally been one of the least automated industries.
sentences.zh: 传统上，建筑业是自动化程度最低的行业之一。

sentences.en: Why is that beginning to change now?
sentences.zh: 为什么现在开始发生变化？

blocks.html_en: I actually think the idea that construction is slow to adopt technology is a bit of a misconception. Builders adopt tools that genuinely make their jobs easier – they've just been waiting for technology that understands how they actually work.

sentences.en: I actually think the idea that construction is slow to adopt technology is a bit of a misconception.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我认为建筑采用技术缓慢的想法有点误解。

sentences.en: Builders adopt tools that genuinely make their jobs easier – they've just been waiting for technology that understands how they actually work.
sentences.zh: 建筑商采用真正让他们的工作变得更轻松的工具——他们只是在等待能够理解他们实际工作方式的技术。

blocks.html_en: Construction is fundamentally different from industries like manufacturing. Every project is unique. Jobsites change every day. Teams are working in environments that are constantly evolving, with dozens of trades operating simultaneously. That's a much harder environment to automate than a factory or warehouse where conditions are highly controlled.

sentences.en: Construction is fundamentally different from industries like manufacturing.
sentences.zh: 建筑业与制造业等行业有着根本的不同。

sentences.en: Every project is unique.
sentences.zh: 每个项目都是独一无二的。

sentences.en: Jobsites change every day.
sentences.zh: 工作地点每天都在变化。

sentences.en: Teams are working in environments that are constantly evolving, with dozens of trades operating simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 团队在不断变化的环境中工作，数十个行业同时运行。

sentences.en: That's a much harder environment to automate than a factory or warehouse where conditions are highly controlled.
sentences.zh: 与条件受到高度控制的工厂或仓库相比，这是一个更难实现自动化的环境。

blocks.html_en: For a long time, most construction software focused on documents, schedules and reports because that's what computers could understand. But construction isn't really a document problem – it's a physical-world problem. The most important information lives on the jobsite itself: what's been built, what's changed, where work is progressing and where risks are emerging.

sentences.en: For a long time, most construction software focused on documents, schedules and reports because that's what computers could understand.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，大多数建筑软件都专注于文档、时间表和报告，因为这是计算机可以理解的。

sentences.en: But construction isn't really a document problem – it's a physical-world problem.
sentences.zh: 但构建实际上并不是一个文档问题——它是一个物理世界的问题。

sentences.en: The most important information lives on the jobsite itself: what's been built, what's changed, where work is progressing and where risks are emerging.
sentences.zh: 最重要的信息存在于工地本身：已建成的内容、已更改的内容、工作进展情况以及出现风险的情况。

blocks.html_en: What's changing now is that AI is becoming capable of understanding the physical world. Instead of asking people to manually document what's happening, AI can interpret images and other real-world data to understand the state of a project. That makes robotics and automation much more practical because they fit naturally into how builders already work instead of forcing them to adopt entirely new processes.

sentences.en: What's changing now is that AI is becoming capable of understanding the physical world.
sentences.zh: 现在发生的变化是人工智能正在变得能够理解物理世界。

sentences.en: Instead of asking people to manually document what's happening, AI can interpret images and other real-world data to understand the state of a project.
sentences.zh: 人工智能可以解释图像和其他现实世界的数据来了解项目的状态，而不是要求人们手动记录正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: That makes robotics and automation much more practical because they fit naturally into how builders already work instead of forcing them to adopt entirely new processes.
sentences.zh: 这使得机器人技术和自动化更加实用，因为它们自然地融入了建筑商已有的工作方式，而不是强迫他们采用全新的流程。

blocks.html_en: • Robotics in construction has been discussed for years but has seen relatively limited adoption. What factors are contributing to the increased interest in autonomous and semi-autonomous systems on jobsites today?

sentences.en: Robotics in construction has been discussed for years but has seen relatively limited adoption.
sentences.zh: 建筑机器人技术已被讨论多年，但应用相对有限。

sentences.en: What factors are contributing to the increased interest in autonomous and semi-autonomous systems on jobsites today?
sentences.zh: 如今，哪些因素导致人们对工作现场的自主和半自主系统越来越感兴趣？

blocks.html_en: The conversation has become much more practical.

sentences.en: The conversation has become much more practical.
sentences.zh: 谈话变得更加实际。

blocks.html_en: Ten years ago, people asked whether robots would replace construction workers or build entire buildings autonomously. Today the question is much simpler: How can robots help experienced builders work more efficiently? That's an important shift because construction has always adopted tools that solve real problems.

sentences.en: Ten years ago, people asked whether robots would replace construction workers or build entire buildings autonomously.
sentences.zh: 十年前，人们问机器人是否会取代建筑工人或自主建造整栋建筑。

sentences.en: Today the question is much simpler: How can robots help experienced builders work more efficiently?
sentences.zh: 今天的问题变得更加简单：机器人如何帮助经验丰富的建筑商更高效地工作？

sentences.en: That's an important shift because construction has always adopted tools that solve real problems.
sentences.zh: 这是一个重要的转变，因为建筑业始终采用解决实际问题的工具。

blocks.html_en: The biggest opportunities today are around repetitive, time-consuming tasks like documenting progress, capturing site conditions or performing routine inspections. Those activities are incredibly valuable, but they're not necessarily the best use of a superintendent's or project engineer's time.

sentences.en: The biggest opportunities today are around repetitive, time-consuming tasks like documenting progress, capturing site conditions or performing routine inspections.
sentences.zh: 当今最大的机会是重复、耗时的任务，例如记录进度、捕获现场情况或执行例行检查。

sentences.en: Those activities are incredibly valuable, but they're not necessarily the best use of a superintendent's or project engineer's time.
sentences.zh: 这些活动非常有价值，但它们不一定是主管或项目工程师时间的最佳利用。

blocks.html_en: I think of robotics a bit like the introduction of nail guns. Nail guns didn't replace carpenters – they helped carpenters work faster and more consistently. Robotics is following a similar path. The goal isn't to automate construction. It's to automate specific tasks that allow skilled professionals to spend more time coordinating work, solving problems and making decisions.

sentences.en: I think of robotics a bit like the introduction of nail guns.
sentences.zh: 我认为机器人技术有点像射钉枪的引入。

sentences.en: Nail guns didn't replace carpenters – they helped carpenters work faster and more consistently.
sentences.zh: 钉枪并没有取代木匠——它们帮助木匠更快、更一致地工作。

sentences.en: Robotics is following a similar path.
sentences.zh: 机器人技术也走着类似的道路。

sentences.en: The goal isn't to automate construction.
sentences.zh: 目标不是自动化施工。

sentences.en: It's to automate specific tasks that allow skilled professionals to spend more time coordinating work, solving problems and making decisions.
sentences.zh: 它使特定任务自动化，让熟练的专业人员能够花更多时间协调工作、解决问题和做出决策。

blocks.html_en: We're already seeing that with the robotics companies that we integrate with, each approaching different aspects of autonomy. Rather than trying to solve every problem, they're proving that robots can reliably perform specific tasks that create immediate value on today's jobsites.

sentences.en: We're already seeing that with the robotics companies that we integrate with, each approaching different aspects of autonomy.
sentences.zh: 我们已经在与我们整合的机器人公司中看到这一点，每个公司都在实现自主性的不同方面。

sentences.en: Rather than trying to solve every problem, they're proving that robots can reliably perform specific tasks that create immediate value on today's jobsites.
sentences.zh: 他们不是试图解决每个问题，而是证明机器人可以可靠地执行特定任务，为当今的工作现场创造直接价值。

blocks.html_en: • Data centers and other large-scale projects have been cited as promising early use cases for construction robotics. What characteristics make those environments more suitable for autonomous technologies?

sentences.en: Data centers and other large-scale projects have been cited as promising early use cases for construction robotics.
sentences.zh: 数据中心和其他大型项目被认为是建筑机器人技术有前景的早期用例。

sentences.en: What characteristics make those environments more suitable for autonomous technologies?
sentences.zh: 哪些特征使这些环境更适合自主技术？

blocks.html_en: Data centers are actually a great example of where robotics and AI can demonstrate value today because they combine three characteristics that work well for autonomous systems.

sentences.en: Data centers are actually a great example of where robotics and AI can demonstrate value today because they combine three characteristics that work well for autonomous systems.
sentences.zh: 数据中心实际上是机器人和人工智能今天可以展示价值的一个很好的例子，因为它们结合了适合自主系统的三个特征。

blocks.html_en: First, they're relatively structured environments. Compared to a renovation project or an occupied hospital, data centers typically have large floor plates, repeatable layouts and fewer unexpected obstacles, making them easier for robots to navigate.

sentences.en: First, they're relatively structured environments.
sentences.zh: 首先，它们是相对结构化的环境。

sentences.en: Compared to a renovation project or an occupied hospital, data centers typically have large floor plates, repeatable layouts and fewer unexpected obstacles, making them easier for robots to navigate.
sentences.zh: 与改造项目或占用的医院相比，数据中心通常拥有较大的地板、可重复的布局和较少的意外障碍，使机器人更容易导航。

blocks.html_en: Second, they're incredibly schedule-sensitive. AI infrastructure is expanding at an unprecedented pace, and every day matters. Owners and contractors need continuous visibility into progress because hundreds of activities are happening simultaneously.

sentences.en: Second, they're incredibly schedule-sensitive.
sentences.zh: 其次，他们对日程安排非常敏感。

sentences.en: AI infrastructure is expanding at an unprecedented pace, and every day matters.
sentences.zh: 人工智能基础设施正在以前所未有的速度扩展，每一天都很重要。

sentences.en: Owners and contractors need continuous visibility into progress because hundreds of activities are happening simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 业主和承包商需要持续了解进度，因为数百项活动同时发生。

blocks.html_en: Finally, they're highly repetitive. The same systems and construction sequences occur over and over, which allows robotics to operate more consistently and makes it easier to measure progress over time.

sentences.en: Finally, they're highly repetitive.
sentences.zh: 最后，它们是高度重复的。

sentences.en: The same systems and construction sequences occur over and over, which allows robotics to operate more consistently and makes it easier to measure progress over time.
sentences.zh: 相同的系统和构建顺序一遍又一遍地发生，这使得机器人能够更加一致地运行，并且更容易衡量随着时间的推移的进展。

blocks.html_en: Autonomous data capture is particularly valuable in these environments because it creates a consistent visual record without disrupting work during the day. That gives project teams objective information about what's actually happening on site, helping them identify issues earlier, coordinate more effectively and keep stakeholders aligned.

sentences.en: Autonomous data capture is particularly valuable in these environments because it creates a consistent visual record without disrupting work during the day.
sentences.zh: 自主数据采集在这些环境中特别有价值，因为它可以创建一致的视觉记录，而不会中断白天的工作。

sentences.en: That gives project teams objective information about what's actually happening on site, helping them identify issues earlier, coordinate more effectively and keep stakeholders aligned.
sentences.zh: 这为项目团队提供了有关现场实际情况的客观信息，帮助他们更早地发现问题、更有效地协调并使利益相关者保持一致。

blocks.html_en: • Construction sites are highly dynamic environments. What are some of the biggest technical and operational challenges robots face when deployed on active projects?

sentences.en: Construction sites are highly dynamic environments.
sentences.zh: 建筑工地是高度动态的环境。

sentences.en: What are some of the biggest technical and operational challenges robots face when deployed on active projects?
sentences.zh: 机器人在部署到活跃项目中时面临哪些最大的技术和操作挑战？

blocks.html_en: Construction sites are probably one of the hardest environments you could ask an autonomous system to operate in.

sentences.en: Construction sites are probably one of the hardest environments you could ask an autonomous system to operate in.
sentences.zh: 建筑工地可能是自治系统运行最困难的环境之一。

blocks.html_en: Unlike a warehouse, where everything is designed to be predictable, construction sites change constantly. Materials move. Equipment gets relocated. Walls appear. Doors that were open yesterday might be closed today. You also have dozens or sometimes hundreds of people working alongside autonomous systems, so safety has to remain the highest priority.

sentences.en: Unlike a warehouse, where everything is designed to be predictable, construction sites change constantly.
sentences.zh: 与仓库的一切设计都是可预测的不同，建筑工地不断变化。

sentences.en: Materials move.
sentences.zh: 材料移动。

sentences.en: Equipment gets relocated.
sentences.zh: 设备被重新安置。

sentences.en: Walls appear.
sentences.zh: 墙壁出现。

sentences.en: Doors that were open yesterday might be closed today.
sentences.zh: 昨天打开的门今天可能会关闭。

sentences.en: You also have dozens or sometimes hundreds of people working alongside autonomous systems, so safety has to remain the highest priority.
sentences.zh: 您还需要数十甚至数百人与自主系统一起工作，因此安全仍然是重中之重。

blocks.html_en: There are practical challenges as well. Connectivity isn't always reliable. GPS often doesn't work indoors. Navigation has to account for changing layouts and temporary obstacles that don't exist in more controlled environments.

sentences.en: There are practical challenges as well.
sentences.zh: 也存在实际挑战。

sentences.en: Connectivity isn't always reliable.
sentences.zh: 连接并不总是可靠的。

sentences.en: GPS often doesn't work indoors.
sentences.zh: GPS 通常在室内不起作用。

sentences.en: Navigation has to account for changing layouts and temporary obstacles that don't exist in more controlled environments.
sentences.zh: 导航必须考虑到变化的布局和临时障碍物，这些在更受控制的环境中不存在。

blocks.html_en: That's why I think we'll continue seeing supervised autonomy for quite some time. Humans are still remarkably good at adapting to unexpected situations, and construction has plenty of them.

sentences.en: That's why I think we'll continue seeing supervised autonomy for quite some time.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为我们将在相当长的一段时间内继续看到受监督的自治。

sentences.en: Humans are still remarkably good at adapting to unexpected situations, and construction has plenty of them.
sentences.zh: 人类仍然非常善于适应意外情况，建筑业也有很多这样的能力。

blocks.html_en: One lesson we've learned is that "good enough" often beats "technically perfect." Builders don't need the most sophisticated robot, they need one that's reliable enough to show up every day, operate safely and consistently, and fit into the way projects already run.

sentences.en: One lesson we've learned is that "good enough" often beats "technically perfect."
sentences.zh: 我们学到的一个教训是“足够好”往往胜过“技术完美”。

sentences.en: Builders don't need the most sophisticated robot, they need one that's reliable enough to show up every day, operate safely and consistently, and fit into the way projects already run.
sentences.zh: 建筑商不需要最复杂的机器人，他们需要的是一个足够可靠、能够每天出现、安全、一致地运行、并适合现有项目运行方式的机器人。

blocks.html_en: • As robotics adoption grows, what role does visual intelligence play in helping machines understand and navigate the physical world?

sentences.en: As robotics adoption grows, what role does visual intelligence play in helping machines understand and navigate the physical world?
sentences.zh: 随着机器人技术的普及，视觉智能在帮助机器理解和导航物理世界方面发挥什么作用？

blocks.html_en: Whether imagery comes from a person carrying a 360° camera, a robot, a drone or another autonomous system, collecting the data is really only the first step. The real challenge is understanding what that data means.

sentences.en: Whether imagery comes from a person carrying a 360° camera, a robot, a drone or another autonomous system, collecting the data is really only the first step.
sentences.zh: 无论图像来自携带 360° 相机的人、机器人、无人机还是其他自主系统，收集数据实际上只是第一步。

sentences.en: The real challenge is understanding what that data means.
sentences.zh: 真正的挑战是理解这些数据的含义。

blocks.html_en: AI has become remarkably good at understanding language, but if it's going to operate in the real-world economy, it also needs to understand physical places, physical assets and physical work.

sentences.en: AI has become remarkably good at understanding language, but if it's going to operate in the real-world economy, it also needs to understand physical places, physical assets and physical work.
sentences.zh: 人工智能已经非常擅长理解语言，但如果它要在现实世界经济中运作，它还需要理解物理地点、物理资产和物理工作。

blocks.html_en: Construction has always had information about what was supposed to happen – drawings, BIM models, schedules and specifications. What's historically been much harder is understanding what actually happened in the field.

sentences.en: Construction has always had information about what was supposed to happen – drawings, BIM models, schedules and specifications.
sentences.zh: 施工始终拥有有关应该发生的事情的信息 - 图纸、BIM 模型、进度表和规格。

sentences.en: What's historically been much harder is understanding what actually happened in the field.
sentences.zh: 从历史上看，理解该领域实际发生的事情要困难得多。

blocks.html_en: That's where visual intelligence comes in. AI can compare what's been built against what was intended to be built, measure progress over time, identify potential issues and surface insights that help project teams make better decisions.

sentences.en: That's where visual intelligence comes in.
sentences.zh: 这就是视觉智能的用武之地。

sentences.en: AI can compare what's been built against what was intended to be built, measure progress over time, identify potential issues and surface insights that help project teams make better decisions.
sentences.zh: 人工智能可以将已构建的内容与预期构建的内容进行比较，衡量一段时间内的进度，识别潜在问题并提供洞察力，帮助项目团队做出更好的决策。

blocks.html_en: Our philosophy is simple: we don't really care how the data gets collected. Whether it comes from a phone, a 360° camera, a drone, a laser scanner or a robotics platform from one of our robotics partners, our goal is to bring that information together into a common understanding of the jobsite.

sentences.en: Our philosophy is simple: we don't really care how the data gets collected.
sentences.zh: 我们的理念很简单：我们并不真正关心数据是如何收集的。

sentences.en: Whether it comes from a phone, a 360° camera, a drone, a laser scanner or a robotics platform from one of our robotics partners, our goal is to bring that information together into a common understanding of the jobsite.
sentences.zh: 无论是来自手机、360° 相机、无人机、激光扫描仪还是来自我们机器人合作伙伴的机器人平台，我们的目标都是将这些信息整合到一起，形成对工作现场的共同理解。

blocks.html_en: Today, our customers have captured imagery across more than 70 billion square feet of construction. That scale creates an opportunity not only to help builders today, but also to help train and validate the next generation of AI systems that need to understand the physical world.

sentences.en: Today, our customers have captured imagery across more than 70 billion square feet of construction.
sentences.zh: 如今，我们的客户已经捕获了超过 700 亿平方英尺的建筑图像。

sentences.en: That scale creates an opportunity not only to help builders today, but also to help train and validate the next generation of AI systems that need to understand the physical world.
sentences.zh: 这种规模不仅为当今的构建者创造了机会，而且还帮助训练和验证需要理解物理世界的下一代人工智能系统。

blocks.html_en: • There's often concern that robotics could replace workers. How are builders currently thinking about the relationship between automation and the existing construction workforce?

sentences.en: There's often concern that robotics could replace workers.
sentences.zh: 人们常常担心机器人可能会取代工人。

sentences.en: How are builders currently thinking about the relationship between automation and the existing construction workforce?
sentences.zh: 建筑商目前如何考虑自动化与现有建筑劳动力之间的关系？

blocks.html_en: I think that's a very understandable concern, but it doesn't reflect what we're seeing on jobsites.

sentences.en: I think that's a very understandable concern, but it doesn't reflect what we're seeing on jobsites.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常可以理解的担忧，但它并不能反映我们在工作现场看到的情况。

blocks.html_en: The builders we work with aren't trying to replace experienced people. If anything, they're trying to figure out how to help those people do more.

sentences.en: The builders we work with aren't trying to replace experienced people.
sentences.zh: 与我们合作的建筑商并不是试图取代有经验的人。

sentences.en: If anything, they're trying to figure out how to help those people do more.
sentences.zh: 如果有的话，他们正在试图找出如何帮助这些人做得更多。

blocks.html_en: Construction has faced labor shortages for decades, and demand continues to outpace the available workforce. There simply aren't enough skilled people entering the trades to meet the amount of work that needs to get done. That's especially true as we build more data centers, manufacturing facilities and infrastructure.

sentences.en: Construction has faced labor shortages for decades, and demand continues to outpace the available workforce.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，建筑业一直面临劳动力短缺的问题，而且需求持续超过可用劳动力。

sentences.en: There simply aren't enough skilled people entering the trades to meet the amount of work that needs to get done.
sentences.zh: 根本没有足够的技术人员进入该行业来满足需要完成的工作量。

sentences.en: That's especially true as we build more data centers, manufacturing facilities and infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 当我们建造更多的数据中心、制造设施和基础设施时尤其如此。

blocks.html_en: Robotics and AI help address that challenge by taking on repetitive work like routine documentation, progress capture or inspections, allowing experienced professionals to spend more time coordinating work, solving problems and applying their expertise.

sentences.en: Robotics and AI help address that challenge by taking on repetitive work like routine documentation, progress capture or inspections, allowing experienced professionals to spend more time coordinating work, solving problems and applying their expertise.
sentences.zh: 机器人和人工智能通过承担例行记录、进度捕获或检查等重复性工作来帮助应对这一挑战，让经验丰富的专业人员能够花更多时间协调工作、解决问题和应用他们的专业知识。

blocks.html_en: The best technology doesn't replace people – it amplifies what people are already good at. That's how I think construction will continue to adopt AI-powered tools and robotics. They become another set of tools that help experienced teams make better decisions, work more efficiently and get more done with the resources they already have.

sentences.en: The best technology doesn't replace people – it amplifies what people are already good at.
sentences.zh: 最好的技术不会取代人类——它会增强人们已经擅长的领域。

sentences.en: That's how I think construction will continue to adopt AI-powered tools and robotics.
sentences.zh: 这就是我认为建筑业将继续采用人工智能驱动的工具和机器人技术的方式。

sentences.en: They become another set of tools that help experienced teams make better decisions, work more efficiently and get more done with the resources they already have.
sentences.zh: 它们成为另一套工具，可以帮助经验丰富的团队做出更好的决策、更高效地工作并利用现有资源完成更多工作。

blocks.html_en: • The concept of "human-in-the-loop" robotics is gaining attention across industries. How does that approach apply within construction environments?

sentences.en: The concept of "human-in-the-loop" robotics is gaining attention across industries.

content_html_zh:
在人工智能和自动化日益占据主导地位的时代，仍然令人难以置信的是有多少建筑工作仍然是手工完成的。 这种对比在数据中心最为明显——数据中心是为支持尖端技术而构建的设施，但其交付通常仍然因主要碎片和耗时的手动任务而减慢。

该行业最大的挑战之一似乎是捕捉和理解项目中实际发生的情况。 项目经理可以花费无数时间走访现场，检查已完成的工作并协调承包商按照不同的时间表进行操作。 当文档落后时，小问题可能会被忽视，并最终发展为代价高昂的延误。

虽然该行业终于开始掌握这项技术，但建筑业也面临着挑战。 自治在固定参数和有限数量的变量下效果最好，但实时站点却提供相反的效果——改变计划、移动材料、建造新结构以及相互协作的多个行业。

建筑业是自动化失败的地方——现在是转折点吗？

这些正是导致自动化在施工中无效的具体条件。 但自动化并非不切实际或不可能，它只是意味着供应商需要专注于机器可以提供最佳结果的任务。

进度捕获、辅助文档和例行检查是自动化最有效的一些领域，更好的是，OpenSpace 等公司认为，大部分工作实际上可以在正常工作时间之外完成，以减少干扰，并减少暴露在实时动态环境中。

数据中心可能是一个很好的试验场，因为它具有大的平面图、可重复的布局和巨大的进度压力。 例如，通过隔夜检查的最新数据，领导者可以评估进展并确定需要额外关注的领域。

但收集这些数据只是第一步，因为在幕后运行的人工智能需要能够解释现场图像，以将其与其他系统中保存的现场平面图、图纸、时间表和其他信息进行交叉引用。

在本次问答中，OpenSpace 首席执行官 Jeevan Kalanithi 解释了为什么建筑自动化开始获得发展势头，为什么“足够好”可能确实足够好而无需立即完善，以及自动化监控如何真正帮助缓解持续劳动力短缺的打击。

  • 传统上，建筑业是自动化程度最低的行业之一。 为什么现在开始发生变化？

实际上，我认为建筑采用技术缓慢的想法有点误解。 建筑商采用真正让他们的工作变得更轻松的工具——他们只是在等待能够理解他们实际工作方式的技术。

建筑业与制造业等行业有着根本的不同。 每个项目都是独一无二的。 工作地点每天都在变化。 团队在不断变化的环境中工作，数十个行业同时运行。 与条件受到高度控制的工厂或仓库相比，这是一个更难实现自动化的环境。

长期以来，大多数建筑软件都专注于文档、时间表和报告，因为这是计算机可以理解的。 但构建实际上并不是一个文档问题——它是一个物理世界的问题。 最重要的信息存在于工地本身：已建成的内容、已更改的内容、工作进展情况以及出现风险的情况。

现在发生的变化是人工智能正在变得能够理解物理世界。 人工智能可以解释图像和其他现实世界的数据来了解项目的状态，而不是要求人们手动记录正在发生的事情。 这使得机器人技术和自动化更加实用，因为它们自然地融入了建筑商已有的工作方式，而不是强迫他们采用全新的流程。

  • 建筑机器人技术已被讨论多年，但应用相对有限。 如今，哪些因素导致人们对工作现场的自主和半自主系统越来越感兴趣？

谈话变得更加实际。

十年前，人们问机器人是否会取代建筑工人或自主建造整栋建筑。 今天的问题变得更加简单：机器人如何帮助经验丰富的建筑商更高效地工作？ 这是一个重要的转变，因为建筑业始终采用解决实际问题的工具。

当今最大的机会是重复、耗时的任务，例如记录进度、捕获现场情况或执行例行检查。 这些活动非常有价值，但它们不一定是主管或项目工程师时间的最佳利用。

我认为机器人技术有点像射钉枪的引入。 钉枪并没有取代木匠——它们帮助木匠更快、更一致地工作。 机器人技术也走着类似的道路。 目标不是自动化施工。 它使特定任务自动化，让熟练的专业人员能够花更多时间协调工作、解决问题和做出决策。

我们已经在与我们整合的机器人公司中看到这一点，每个公司都在实现自主性的不同方面。 他们不是试图解决每个问题，而是证明机器人可以可靠地执行特定任务，为当今的工作现场创造直接价值。

  • 数据中心和其他大型项目被认为是建筑机器人技术有前景的早期用例。 哪些特征使这些环境更适合自主技术？

数据中心实际上是机器人和人工智能今天可以展示价值的一个很好的例子，因为它们结合了适合自主系统的三个特征。

首先，它们是相对结构化的环境。 与改造项目或占用的医院相比，数据中心通常拥有较大的地板、可重复的布局和较少的意外障碍，使机器人更容易导航。

其次，他们对日程安排非常敏感。 人工智能基础设施正在以前所未有的速度扩展，每一天都很重要。 业主和承包商需要持续了解进度，因为数百项活动同时发生。

最后，它们是高度重复的。 相同的系统和构建顺序一遍又一遍地发生，这使得机器人能够更加一致地运行，并且更容易衡量随着时间的推移的进展。

自主数据采集在这些环境中特别有价值，因为它可以创建一致的视觉记录，而不会中断白天的工作。 这为项目团队提供了有关现场实际情况的客观信息，帮助他们更早地发现问题、更有效地协调并使利益相关者保持一致。

  • 建筑工地是高度动态的环境。 机器人在部署到活跃项目中时面临哪些最大的技术和操作挑战？

建筑工地可能是自治系统运行最困难的环境之一。

与仓库的一切设计都是可预测的不同，建筑工地不断变化。 材料移动。 设备被重新安置。 墙壁出现。 昨天打开的门今天可能会关闭。 您还需要数十甚至数百人与自主系统一起工作，因此安全仍然是重中之重。

也存在实际挑战。 连接并不总是可靠的。 GPS 通常在室内不起作用。 导航必须考虑到变化的布局和临时障碍物，这些在更受控制的环境中不存在。

这就是为什么我认为我们将在相当长的一段时间内继续看到受监督的自治。 人类仍然非常善于适应意外情况，建筑业也有很多这样的能力。

我们学到的一个教训是“足够好”往往胜过“技术完美”。 建筑商不需要最复杂的机器人，他们需要的是一个足够可靠、能够每天出现、安全、一致地运行、并适合现有项目运行方式的机器人。

  • 随着机器人技术的普及，视觉智能在帮助机器理解和导航物理世界方面发挥什么作用？

无论图像来自携带 360° 相机的人、机器人、无人机还是其他自主系统，收集数据实际上只是第一步。 真正的挑战是理解这些数据的含义。

人工智能已经非常擅长理解语言，但如果它要在现实世界经济中运作，它还需要理解物理地点、物理资产和物理工作。

施工始终拥有有关应该发生的事情的信息 - 图纸、BIM 模型、进度表和规格。 从历史上看，理解该领域实际发生的事情要困难得多。

这就是视觉智能的用武之地。 人工智能可以将已构建的内容与预期构建的内容进行比较，衡量一段时间内的进度，识别潜在问题并提供洞察力，帮助项目团队做出更好的决策。

我们的理念很简单：我们并不真正关心数据是如何收集的。 无论是来自手机、360° 相机、无人机、激光扫描仪还是来自我们机器人合作伙伴的机器人平台，我们的目标都是将这些信息整合到一起，形成对工作现场的共同理解。

如今，我们的客户已经捕获了超过 700 亿平方英尺的建筑图像。 这种规模不仅为当今的构建者创造了机会，而且还帮助训练和验证需要理解物理世界的下一代人工智能系统。

  • 人们常常担心机器人可能会取代工人。 建筑商目前如何考虑自动化与现有建筑劳动力之间的关系？

我认为这是一个非常可以理解的担忧，但它并不能反映我们在工作现场看到的情况。

与我们合作的建筑商并不是试图取代有经验的人。 如果有的话，他们正在试图找出如何帮助这些人做得更多。

几十年来，建筑业一直面临劳动力短缺的问题，而且需求持续超过可用劳动力。 根本没有足够的技术人员进入该行业来满足需要完成的工作量。 当我们建造更多的数据中心、制造设施和基础设施时尤其如此。

机器人和人工智能通过承担例行记录、进度捕获或检查等重复性工作来帮助应对这一挑战，让经验丰富的专业人员能够花更多时间协调工作、解决问题和应用他们的专业知识。

最好的技术不会取代人类——它会增强人们已经擅长的领域。 这就是我认为建筑业将继续采用人工智能驱动的工具和机器人技术的方式。 它们成为另一套工具，可以帮助经验丰富的团队做出更好的决策、更高效地工作并利用现有资源完成更多工作。

  • “人机交互”机器人技术的概念正在引起各行业的关注。 该方法如何应用于施工环境？

我认为“人机交互”将在相当长一段时间内成为建筑的主导模式。

施工的动态性太大，无法指望完全自主的系统能够处理所有情况。 每天都会发生一些意想不到的事情——走廊被堵塞、设备被搬迁、新的安全屏障、突然无法进入的区域。 人类仍然非常善于识别这些情况并实时适应。

我们今天看到的是非常实际的责任划分。 机器人始终如一地处理日常重复性任务，而人们则在需要时提供判断、背景和干预。

我们的一些机器人合作伙伴已经采用这种方式进行操作，其中自主系统执行大部分工作，但仍保持远程监督，以便在发生意外情况时有人可以介入。

我不认为这是一个妥协。 我认为这实际上是正确的模型。 目标不是为了自治本身。 目标是为项目团队提供更好的信息，同时保持复杂建设项目所需的灵活性和判断力。

  • 一些承包商正在尝试在非工作时间（例如夜间或工作人员到达之前）进行自主数据采集。 从这些早期部署中汲取了哪些经验教训？

最大的教训是一致性。

手动文档的挑战之一是它取决于人们是否有时间去做。 在繁忙的项目中，文档很容易成为较低的优先级，因为每个人都专注于解决眼前的问题。

自主捕获改变了这一点。 机器人可以按照可预测的时间表记录现场，通常是在夜间或工作人员到达之前，每天创建一致的视觉记录，而不会中断施工活动。

这种一致性使团队能够更清楚地了解项目随时间的进展情况。 它还使文档更具弹性。 如果当天主管有事或项目工程师外出，视觉记录也不会停止。 每个人仍然可以访问有关现场正在发生的事情的最新信息。

捕捉视觉记录一直是使用 360° 相机行走现场的自然副产品。 这也是一个非常自然的交给机器人的任务。 这使得有经验的人能够花更多的时间解释信息和做出决策，而不是简单地收集数据。

  • 展望未来，行业应该关注哪些指标，以更好地了解建筑机器人技术是否正在超越试点计划并走向更广泛的采用？

我认为最大的指标不是工作现场的机器人数量。 问题在于试点结束后承包商是否继续使用它们。

建筑业是一个实践性很强的行业。 建筑商采用技术并不是因为它令人兴奋，而是因为它可以节省时间、降低风险或帮助项目更顺利地运行。 如果一项技术创造的工作多于它消除的工作，那么它就不会持久。

当机器人技术成为收集项目信息的另一种方式时，我们还将知道该行业已进入下一阶段。 构建者不必考虑数据是否来自人、机器人、无人机或其他自主系统。 他们应该能够准确、最新地了解其项目中发生的情况。

最终，我认为这个故事比机器人技术更重要。 现实世界的经济不仅仅依靠文件来运行。 它运行在物理场所、物理资产和物理工作上。 如果人工智能要在那里创造价值，它必须理解现实，而不仅仅是语言。

这就是为什么我们说特工需要眼睛。 当人工智能能够可靠地看到、理解和推理物理世界中发生的事情时，机器人技术就不再是自动化了。 它成为人们与建筑环境互动并做出更好决策的新方式。 我认为这就是我们未来十年将讨论的转变。
